title: Police wrap up probe into fatal shooting of Kuol
article: City police have completed their investigation into the fatal police shooting of Deng Kuol, though it could be months before the man's family has answers.

The case has been turned over to the Edmonton Crown prosecutors' office for further inquiry, and an internal investigation by the Calgary Police Service's professional standards section will begin soon after.
"It's been sent there for an unbiased, independent review," said homicide unit Staff Sgt. Barry Cochran, who is withholding Calgary's findings until the Edmonton investigation is finished.
"They're going to review the file and get back to us with disposition," said Cochran.
Deng Fermino Kuol, 34, was shot by Const. Ira Macumber on Oct. 25, after a scuffle outside an apartment building at 1709 37th St. S.E.
Kuol was sitting outside the residence when Macumber arrived.
Investigators said that after initially agreeing to leave, Kuol drew a knife and slashed the officer in the left bicep.
Macumber struggled to restrain his attacker, then pulled his gun and fired twice -- in keeping with officer training, according to police.

The shooting sparked outrage from members of Calgary's Sudanese community, who hope to address some of their concerns at a public fatality inquiry, which does not make any legal findings or assign blame, and will begin as soon as all other investigations are complete.
"Our lawyer will work very hard to find out what happened," said Martin Yak, chairman of the Sudanese Community Relations Committee.
"We will never be satisfied with a police investigation."
Cochran said in cases involving a police officer, it's standard procedure for the investigation to be passed on to an external agency.
The Edmonton investigation is expected to take about a month and could recommend charges against Macumber, who returned to work two weeks after the incident.
Any disciplinary action will be decided by the professional standards section of the city police.
